name: OpenHands (formerly OpenDevin)
description: AI-driven development platform. Composable Python SDK for building coding agents that can modify code, run commands, browse web, call APIs. Supports local or cloud execution at scale (1000s of agents). V1 architecture with optional isolation, stateless design, and two-layer composability.
input_format: GitHub issues, natural language instructions, CLI prompts
output_format: Code patches, pull requests, terminal output
verification_method: Test execution in sandboxed Docker environments, SWE-bench evaluation (50%+ solve rate)
human_gates: Approval-based in CLI mode; asynchronous PR review in cloud mode
agent_architecture: Single agent with tool-use loop; SDK supports custom multi-agent compositions. CodeAct agent as default. Sandboxed execution environments.
execution_model: Event-driven agent loop with tool calls. Docker sandbox isolation. Local CLI or cloud-hosted agent server.
strengths: Most mature open-source AI developer platform with 65K+ stars
Composable SDK enables custom agent architectures
Docker sandbox isolation for safe execution
Enterprise directory with RBAC and SSO
Active community with hundreds of contributors
weaknesses: No structured spec-to-code pipeline - primarily issue-driven
Limited built-in planning/decomposition for large features
No formal verification layers beyond test execution
No persistent knowledge/learning system across sessions
No structured human gates between phases
comparison_to_forge: OpenHands is broader but shallower in the spec-to-code pipeline. It excels at ad-hoc issue resolution but lacks Forge's structured phases (requirements -> plan -> execute -> verify), 8-layer verification engine, session ledger for cross-wave knowledge propagation, and assessment/splitting pipeline for context management.

name: SWE-agent
description: Academic research project from Princeton/Stanford that autonomously fixes GitHub issues using a custom Agent-Computer Interface (ACI). State-of-the-art on SWE-bench among open-source projects. Configurable via single YAML file. Designed for research - simple and hackable.
input_format: GitHub issues, bug reports, natural language task descriptions
output_format: Git patches, code diffs
verification_method: Test suite execution, SWE-bench evaluation. SWE-ReX sandbox for isolated code execution.
human_gates: None - fully autonomous execution. Results reviewed post-hoc.
agent_architecture: Single agent with custom ACI (Agent-Computer Interface) for repository browsing, viewing, editing, and executing code. Tool-based approach with LLM choosing actions.
execution_model: Sequential agent loop. Single issue at a time. SWE-ReX provides sandboxed execution locally or in cloud. YAML-configurable.
strengths: State-of-the-art SWE-bench performance among open-source tools
Custom ACI optimized for LLM-code interaction
SWE-ReX sandbox for safe parallel execution
Model-agnostic - works with GPT-4o, Claude, etc.
weaknesses: No planning or decomposition - single-issue focused
No persistent knowledge or session state
Research tool, not production engineering pipeline
comparison_to_forge: SWE-agent is a research tool for autonomous bug fixing, not an engineering pipeline. It excels at single-issue resolution but has no concept of specifications, phased planning, verification layers, knowledge propagation, or human gates. Forge provides the full SDLC structure that SWE-agent lacks.

name: Aider
description: AI pair programming in the terminal. Uses tree-sitter repo maps for whole-codebase awareness. Automatic git commits, multi-file editing, voice coding support. Works with 75+ LLM providers. Architect mode for plan-first development.
input_format: Natural language chat, voice input, image input, URLs
output_format: Direct file edits with automatic git commits
verification_method: Linter/compiler error detection and auto-fix. No built-in test execution pipeline.
human_gates: Interactive chat-based approval. Every change visible before commit. /ask mode for exploration without changes.
agent_architecture: Single agent with repo-map context. Architect mode uses two-model pipeline (architect plans, editor implements). Tree-sitter for code understanding.
execution_model: Interactive REPL. Sequential editing with git integration. Architect mode for plan-then-execute. Can run in scripted/headless mode.
strengths: Massive community (95K+ stars) with excellent documentation
Tree-sitter repo map for whole-codebase context
Automatic git commits with sensible messages
Works with 75+ LLM providers including local models
Voice coding and image input support
weaknesses: No persistent knowledge system across sessions
comparison_to_forge: Aider is an excellent interactive pair programmer but not a structured engineering pipeline. It lacks Forge's phased workflow, multi-agent parallelism, 8-layer verification, assessment/splitting for large tasks, and session continuity. Aider's architect mode is a basic plan-then-execute, while Forge provides full DAG-based wave planning with dependency resolution.

name: MetaGPT
description: Multi-agent framework simulating a software company. Agents play roles (PM, Architect, Engineer, QA) following SOPs. Takes one-line requirement and outputs PRD, design, tasks, and code. Core philosophy: Code = SOP(Team). Evolved into MGX for natural language programming.
input_format: One-line natural language requirement
output_format: PRD, system design, API specs, data structures, complete codebase, documentation
verification_method: QA agent reviews code. Code review between agents. No external test execution pipeline.
human_gates: Minimal - primarily autonomous. Design review possible but not enforced.
agent_architecture: Multi-agent with role-based specialization: ProductManager, Architect, ProjectManager, Engineer, QA. Agents communicate via structured message passing following SOPs. Chat chain coordination.
execution_model: Sequential pipeline: requirement -> PRD -> design -> task decomposition -> implementation -> review. Waterfall-like flow through agent roles.
strengths: Most complete spec-to-code pipeline among open-source tools
Generates PRD, design docs, API specs automatically
SOP-driven methodology mirrors real software teams
weaknesses: Weak verification - no test execution or multi-layer checks
Limited human gates in the pipeline
No context management for large codebases
Development appears to have slowed (last commit Jan 2026)
comparison_to_forge: MetaGPT is the closest philosophical match to Forge in the open-source space - both simulate structured software teams with role-based agents. However, MetaGPT lacks Forge's 8-layer verification engine, session ledger for knowledge propagation, context budget management with assessment/splitting, parallel wave execution with DAG scheduling, and human gates between phases. MetaGPT's verification is limited to agent-level code review.

name: GPT-Engineer
description: CLI platform for AI code generation. Specify what you want, AI asks for clarification, then builds it. Historically significant as one of the first autonomous coding tools (April 2023). Now in maintenance mode - team focused on commercial Lovable.dev product.
input_format: Natural language prompt in text file, optional image inputs
output_format: Complete codebase generation, file structure
verification_method: None built-in. Manual testing required.
human_gates: Clarification questions before generation. No gates during execution.
agent_architecture: Single agent with clarification loop. Generates full codebase in one pass. No multi-agent coordination.
execution_model: Single-shot generation: prompt -> clarify -> generate. No iterative refinement or execution.
weaknesses: In maintenance mode - team moved to Lovable.dev
No persistent knowledge or session state
Cannot work with existing codebases effectively
comparison_to_forge: GPT-Engineer is a generation-only tool with no pipeline structure. It lacks everything that makes Forge an engineering system: phased execution, verification layers, planning, knowledge propagation, parallel execution, and human gates. Effectively deprecated in favor of Lovable.dev.

name: GPT-Pilot (Pythagora)
description: AI developer that builds apps step-by-step like a human developer, with debugging throughout development. Clarifies requirements, writes specs, implements incrementally, and debugs issues as they arise. Core technology behind Pythagora VS Code extension.
input_format: Natural language app description, iterative clarification
output_format: Complete application codebase with step-by-step implementation
verification_method: Self-debugging during development. Human testing prompts at checkpoints. No automated test pipeline.
human_gates: Extensive - asks for approval at each development step, requests testing feedback, clarifies requirements iteratively
agent_architecture: Multi-step agent with specialized phases: specification, architecture, development, debugging. Single agent with different modes rather than multiple agents.
execution_model: Sequential step-by-step development mimicking human workflow. Each step produces working code. Debug loops when issues detected.
strengths: Strong human-in-the-loop design with approval at each step
Step-by-step development mirrors real developer workflow
Produces working applications, not just code snippets
weaknesses: Fair Source License limits commercial use
No parallel execution or multi-agent architecture
Development shifted to commercial Pythagora VS Code extension
comparison_to_forge: GPT-Pilot has the strongest human gate design among open-source tools, similar in spirit to Forge's phase gates. However, it lacks Forge's parallel execution, 8-layer verification, code graph awareness, context budget management, and is focused on greenfield development rather than working with existing codebases.

name: ChatDev
description: Multi-agent collaboration framework simulating a software company. Agents (CEO, CTO, Programmer, Tester) participate in functional seminars to automate the SDLC. ChatDev 2.0 (DevAll) is a zero-code multi-agent platform for diverse tasks beyond software development.
input_format: Natural language software description
output_format: Complete software project with code, documentation, tests
verification_method: Tester agent reviews code. Communicative dehallucination technique. No external test execution.
human_gates: Minimal - primarily autonomous execution. Post-hoc review.
agent_architecture: Multi-agent with role-based specialization (CEO, CTO, Programmer, Reviewer, Tester). Chat chain orchestration. Communicative dehallucination for quality. V2 adds visual workflow designer.
execution_model: Sequential chat chain: design -> coding -> testing -> documenting. Agents communicate in structured dialogues through phases.
strengths: Full SDLC simulation with role-based agents
V2 adds zero-code visual workflow designer
weaknesses: No persistent knowledge or session state
No context management for large codebases
V2 broadened scope away from software engineering focus
comparison_to_forge: ChatDev shares Forge's multi-agent role-based philosophy but implements it as academic research rather than production engineering. It lacks Forge's verification engine, session ledger, context budget management, DAG-based parallel execution, and human gates. ChatDev 2.0 has moved toward general-purpose multi-agent orchestration rather than deepening software engineering capabilities.

name: AutoCodeRover
description: AST-aware autonomous software engineer for program improvement. Searches code context in abstract syntax trees rather than plain string matching. Uses statistical fault localization when test suites available. Resolves GitHub issues at $0.43-0.65 average cost per issue.
input_format: GitHub issues, bug reports
output_format: Git patches in diff format
verification_method: Test suite execution, statistical fault localization, patch validation. Multi-patch generation with ranking.
human_gates: None - fully autonomous. Results reviewed post-hoc.
agent_architecture: Single agent with AST-aware code search. Two-phase: localization (hierarchical file->class->function->location narrowing) then repair (multi-patch generation with filtering/ranking).
execution_model: Sequential: localize -> repair -> validate. Generates multiple candidate patches and ranks them. Interactive mode available.
strengths: AST-aware code search - understands program structure
Statistical fault localization when tests available
weaknesses: GPL-3.0 license may limit commercial adoption
comparison_to_forge: AutoCodeRover is a specialized bug-fixing tool, not an engineering pipeline. Its AST-aware localization is interesting technology that Forge's code graph provides at a deeper level. AutoCodeRover lacks all of Forge's pipeline structure, verification layers, session management, and parallel execution.

name: Agentless
description: Non-agent approach to automated software repair from UIUC. Simple three-phase pipeline: localization, repair, patch validation. Demonstrates that structured non-agent approaches can match or exceed complex agent systems. Low cost at $0.70 per fix.
input_format: GitHub issues, bug descriptions
output_format: Git patches in diff format
verification_method: Test-based patch validation, patch ranking and filtering
human_gates: None - fully autonomous pipeline
agent_architecture: No agents - structured pipeline with LLM calls. Three phases: hierarchical localization (file -> class/function -> edit location), repair (multi-patch generation), validation (test execution + ranking).
execution_model: Sequential three-phase pipeline. Non-agentic - no tool use or action loops. Direct LLM prompting with structured output.
strengths: Proves simple pipelines can match complex agents
Clean three-phase architecture - easy to understand
Strong SWE-bench performance (32% lite, 50.8% verified with Claude 3.5)
weaknesses: No agent capabilities - cannot use tools or iterate
comparison_to_forge: Agentless is philosophically interesting as a counterpoint - showing that structured pipelines without agents can work. Forge takes the opposite approach with rich agent orchestration. Agentless's three-phase pipeline (localize-repair-validate) is a minimal version of what Forge does across 8 verification layers and multiple execution waves.

name: Cline (formerly Claude Dev)
description: Autonomous coding agent as VS Code/JetBrains extension. Creates/edits files, executes commands, automates browser interactions with human approval at each step. Model-agnostic, supports any LLM provider. Token tracking and cost monitoring built in.
input_format: Natural language chat in IDE, file context
output_format: Direct file edits, terminal commands, browser actions
verification_method: Linter/compiler error monitoring with proactive fix. No structured verification pipeline.
human_gates: Strong - asks permission for every file edit, command execution, and browser action. Full transparency.
agent_architecture: Single agent with tool use (file edit, terminal, browser). Human-in-the-loop approval for each action. MCP extension support.
execution_model: Interactive agent loop in IDE. Sequential tool use with human approval. Token and cost tracking per task.
strengths: IDE-native experience in VS Code and JetBrains
Browser automation for web development testing
Model-agnostic - works with any LLM provider
weaknesses: No structured pipeline - reactive coding assistant
No planning or decomposition for large tasks
Per-action approval can be tedious for large changes
comparison_to_forge: Cline excels at human oversight (per-action approval) but lacks all pipeline structure. Forge provides structured phases, planning, verification layers, and knowledge propagation that Cline doesn't attempt. Cline is an interactive assistant; Forge is an engineering automation system.

name: Plandex
description: Terminal-based AI coding agent for large projects. Plans and executes multi-step tasks across dozens of files. Cumulative diff review sandbox, full version control for plans, branch exploration. Handles 2M token context with tree-sitter project maps. WINDING DOWN as of Oct 2025.
input_format: Natural language tasks, file context, REPL commands
output_format: Sandboxed diffs (reviewed before applying), git commits
verification_method: Diff review sandbox separates AI changes from project files. Rollback capability. No automated test execution.
human_gates: Strong - cumulative diff review before applying. Branch exploration for comparing approaches. Step-by-step review mode.
agent_architecture: Single agent with plan-execute model. Version-controlled plans with branching. Client-server architecture.
execution_model: Plan-then-execute with sandboxed changes. Full autonomy possible but configurable step-by-step review. Tree-sitter indexing for 20M+ token directories.
strengths: Best sandboxed change management - review before applying
Version control for plans with branching
Large context handling (2M tokens, 20M+ with indexing)
weaknesses: WINDING DOWN - no longer accepting new users (Oct 2025)
comparison_to_forge: Plandex had the most Forge-like planning approach with version-controlled plans and sandboxed changes. Its diff sandbox is conceptually similar to Forge's patch collection from container agents. However, Plandex lacked verification layers, multi-agent execution, and knowledge propagation. Now effectively defunct.

name: Sweep AI
description: AI junior developer that turns GitHub issues into pull requests. Reads repository, plans implementation, writes code, adds tests, creates PRs. Includes sandbox for test execution. Now pivoted to JetBrains IDE plugin.
input_format: GitHub issues with sweep label
output_format: Pull requests with code changes and tests
verification_method: Sandbox test suite execution. Self-fixing on test failure before PR creation.
human_gates: PR review as primary gate. Automated execution between issue and PR.
agent_architecture: Single agent with GitHub integration. Reads codebase, plans, implements, tests, creates PR. Sandbox environment for verification.
execution_model: Event-driven: GitHub issue triggers autonomous pipeline. Sandbox execution for testing. Self-fix loop on failures.
weaknesses: Pivoted to JetBrains plugin - original GitHub bot less maintained
No human gates between planning and execution
comparison_to_forge: Sweep's GitHub integration for issue-to-PR automation is clean but shallow compared to Forge's full pipeline. Sweep's self-fix loop is a basic version of Forge's verification loop with loop detection and escalation. Forge provides deeper planning, multi-layer verification, and cross-wave knowledge propagation.

name: OpenCode
description: The most-starred open-source AI coding agent. Go-based terminal TUI supporting 75+ LLM providers. Built-in build and plan agents. Session management, LSP integration, vim-like editor. Client/server architecture. 6.5M monthly developers.
input_format: Natural language chat in TUI, file context
output_format: Direct file edits, command execution
verification_method: LSP integration for code intelligence. No structured verification pipeline.
human_gates: Interactive chat with approval. Plan agent for read-only analysis before changes.
agent_architecture: Two built-in agents: 'build' (full-access development) and 'plan' (read-only analysis). MCP extension support. Plugin ecosystem.
execution_model: Interactive TUI agent loop. Client/server architecture. SQLite for persistent sessions. Fully offline capable with local models.
strengths: Most popular open-source coding agent (147K stars, 6.5M users)
Built in Go for speed and efficiency
75+ LLM providers including fully offline operation
weaknesses: No multi-agent parallelism for large tasks
Plan agent is read-only, not a real planner
comparison_to_forge: OpenCode is the most popular tool in this space but is fundamentally an interactive coding assistant, not an engineering pipeline. It has no equivalent to Forge's phased workflow, 8-layer verification, assessment/splitting, wave-based parallel execution, or session ledger. OpenCode's 'plan' agent is a read-only explorer, not a real planning system.

name: Superpowers
description: Agentic skills framework and software development methodology. Composable markdown-based skills for coding agents. Enforces brainstorm -> plan -> implement via subagent-driven development with TDD. Each task gets fresh subagent with two-stage review (spec compliance + code quality).
input_format: Natural language design discussions, approved designs
output_format: Implemented code via git worktrees, tested and reviewed
verification_method: Two-stage review per task (spec compliance, code quality). TDD enforcement (red-green-refactor). Test baseline verification.
human_gates: Design validation checkpoints. Batch implementation with human review points. Plan approval before execution.
agent_architecture: Coordinator agent dispatches fresh subagents per task. Each subagent gets only task description and relevant context (prevents context pollution). Skills are composable markdown files. Works with Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex.
execution_model: Brainstorm -> design -> plan (2-5min tasks) -> subagent execution -> two-stage review. Git worktree isolation per task. Supports hours of autonomous operation.
strengths: Most structured development methodology in the space
Two-stage review (spec + quality) for every task
Agent-agnostic - works with Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex
121K stars - second most popular after OpenCode
weaknesses: Methodology framework, not integrated system - depends on host agent
No built-in verification engine (relies on TDD within subagents)
No persistent knowledge/learning system across sessions
comparison_to_forge: Superpowers is the closest methodological match to Forge's philosophy. Both emphasize structured planning, task decomposition, and verification. Key differences: Forge has a built-in 8-layer verification engine vs. Superpowers' TDD-only approach; Forge has session ledger for knowledge propagation; Forge has DAG-based wave scheduling vs. sequential subagent dispatch; Forge has context budget management with assessment/splitting. Superpowers is a methodology layer; Forge is an integrated system.

name: GitHub Spec Kit
description: Toolkit for Spec-Driven Development from GitHub. CLI (specify) and workflow for structured AI-assisted coding: specify -> plan -> tasks -> implement. Agent-agnostic - works with 30+ AI coding tools. Separates 'what' (specs) from 'how' (code). Quality checklists for requirements validation.
input_format: Specifications in markdown, natural language requirements
output_format: Technical plans, task lists, implementation via integrated agents
verification_method: Quality checklists for spec validation. Plan review. Task-level verification criteria. No automated test execution.
human_gates: Checkpoints between each phase: spec review, plan review, task review, implementation review
agent_architecture: No built-in agents - provides scaffolding for external agents. Slash commands integrate with host agents (Copilot, Claude Code, Gemini). Template-driven workflow.
execution_model: Four-phase workflow: specify -> plan -> tasks -> implement. Each phase produces artifacts reviewed by human. Agent-agnostic execution.
strengths: Agent-agnostic - works with 30+ AI coding tools
Strong human gates between each phase
Backed by GitHub with strong documentation
weaknesses: No built-in execution engine - relies on external agents
No parallel execution or resource management
Specification toolkit, not complete engineering system
comparison_to_forge: Spec Kit is the best requirements framework but only a framework - it needs an execution engine. Forge provides the complete pipeline that Spec Kit starts but doesn't finish: verification engine, agent factory, parallel execution planner, session management, and knowledge propagation. Spec Kit's specify->plan->tasks->implement mirrors Forge's requirements->plan->execute->verify but without the execution and verification infrastructure.

name: Intent Integrity Kit (IIKit)
description: Methodology and toolkit for making AI-generated code verifiable from requirements to running software. Uses SHA256 cryptographic hashing to prevent test tampering during implementation. 10-phase workflow from constitution to export. Agent-agnostic with git hook enforcement.
input_format: Specifications, Gherkin .feature files, natural language requirements
output_format: Verified implementation with cryptographic integrity chain
verification_method: SHA256 assertion integrity hashing. Git hook enforcement (pre-commit, post-commit). Prevents circular verification (AI modifying tests to match bugs). Coverage and quality verification.
human_gates: Specification approval before implementation. Feature file locking before coding. Requirements change forces spec revision.
agent_architecture: No built-in agents - provides verification layer for any agent. Agent-agnostic hooks work with Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Gemini, OpenCode.
execution_model: 10-phase pipeline: constitution -> specify -> clarify -> plan -> checklist -> testify -> tasks -> analyze -> implement -> export. Cryptographic verification at each transition.
strengths: Prevents circular verification (AI tampering with tests)
Agent-agnostic - works with any coding agent
Git hook enforcement is infrastructure-level guarantee
weaknesses: No parallel execution or agent orchestration
No persistent knowledge or session management
comparison_to_forge: IIKit has the most sophisticated verification approach in the space - cryptographic integrity chains are stronger than Forge's hash-based contract checks. However, IIKit is a verification overlay, not a complete system. Forge provides the full pipeline (agent factory, parallel planner, container orchestration, session ledger) that IIKit doesn't attempt. The two are complementary - IIKit's cryptographic verification could enhance Forge's verification engine.

name: Codex CLI (OpenAI)
description: OpenAI's terminal-based coding agent built in Rust. Reads, changes, and runs code locally. Supports subagents for parallel tasks, code review agents, web search, MCP tool integration. Slash commands for specialized workflows.
input_format: Natural language prompts, slash commands, MCP tool calls
output_format: Direct file edits, command execution, PR creation
verification_method: Separate review agent for code review before committing. No structured verification pipeline.
human_gates: Configurable autonomy levels. Review agent as automated gate. Interactive approval in default mode.
agent_architecture: Primary agent with subagent spawning for parallelism. MCP integration for tool extensibility. Slash commands for specialized workflows. Built in Rust.
execution_model: Terminal agent loop. Subagents for parallel tasks. MCP servers for tool integration. Supports STDIO and streaming HTTP MCP servers.
strengths: Backed by OpenAI with active development
weaknesses: No persistent knowledge or session state
Primarily interactive assistant, not automation system
Tied to OpenAI models for best experience
comparison_to_forge: Codex CLI is a well-built interactive agent with subagent parallelism, but lacks all pipeline structure. Its subagent model is a primitive version of Forge's wave-based parallel execution. Forge provides structured phases, verification engine, session management, and knowledge propagation that Codex CLI doesn't attempt.

name: Goose (Block)
description: Open-source extensible AI agent from Block (Square). Desktop app + CLI + API. 70+ MCP extensions. Subagent parallelism, prompt injection detection, adversary reviewer. Portable YAML recipes for shareable workflows. 15+ LLM providers.
input_format: Natural language, YAML recipes, MCP tool calls
output_format: File edits, command execution, multi-tool actions
verification_method: Adversary reviewer for safety. Test execution via extensions. No structured verification pipeline.
human_gates: Tool permission controls. Sandbox mode. Configurable autonomy.
agent_architecture: Core agent loop in Rust with provider abstraction, MCP extension system. Subagent spawning for parallel tasks. Adversary reviewer for safety. Recipe system for workflow capture.
execution_model: Plan-execute-evaluate loop. MCP-based tool integration. Subagent parallelism. Desktop, CLI, and API interfaces. YAML recipes for repeatable workflows.
strengths: Most extensible agent with 70+ MCP extensions
Strong security model (injection detection, sandbox, permissions)
weaknesses: Recipe system is not a real planning system
comparison_to_forge: Goose is the most extensible agent in the space (70+ MCP extensions) but is a general-purpose tool, not an engineering pipeline. Its recipe system enables workflow capture but not structured planning. Forge provides the engineering-specific structure (phases, verification, knowledge propagation) that Goose's general framework doesn't provide.

name: Devika
description: Open-source agentic AI software engineer, originally an alternative to Devin. Understands high-level instructions, breaks into steps, researches web, writes code. Supports Claude, GPT-4, and local LLMs via Ollama. Web UI for interaction. Project rebranded to Opcode.
input_format: Natural language high-level instructions
output_format: Complete codebase, project structure
verification_method: None built-in. Manual review required.
human_gates: Web UI interaction. No structured gates.
agent_architecture: Single agent with modular components: Planning/Reasoning engine, Research module (web browsing), Code Writing module, Browser Interaction module. Keyword extraction for research.
execution_model: Sequential: understand -> plan -> research -> code. Web browsing for information gathering. Single-pass generation.
strengths: Web research capability for context gathering
weaknesses: Appears abandoned (last commit March 2025, rebranded to Opcode)
comparison_to_forge: Devika is a first-generation Devin clone that has been effectively abandoned. It lacks all of Forge's engineering pipeline structure, verification, knowledge management, and parallel execution. Its web research capability is interesting but insufficient for structured engineering.

name: Claude Code Agent Farm
description: Orchestration framework for running 20-50+ Claude Code agents in parallel. Automated bug fixing, best-practices sweeps, lock-based coordination. Real-time tmux monitoring dashboard. Supports 34 technology stacks. Adaptive idle timeout and automatic agent recovery.
input_format: Workflow configuration (bug-fix, best-practices), technology stack selection
output_format: Code improvements applied across codebase
verification_method: Lock-based coordination to prevent conflicts. Agent heartbeat monitoring. No formal verification pipeline.
human_gates: Dashboard monitoring. Post-hoc review of changes.
agent_architecture: Orchestrator spawns 20-50+ Claude Code agents in parallel tmux sessions. Lock-based coordination prevents file conflicts. Context warnings and heartbeat tracking.
execution_model: Parallel agent farm with tmux sessions. Lock-based file coordination. Automatic agent recovery on failure. Adaptive idle timeout.
comparison_to_forge: Agent Farm provides brute-force parallelism (many Claude Code instances) while Forge provides structured parallelism (DAG-based wave planning with dependency resolution). Agent Farm's lock-based coordination is simpler than Forge's resource-aware bin-packing. Forge's knowledge propagation between waves is absent from Agent Farm.

name: ComposioHQ Agent Orchestrator
description: Agentic orchestrator for parallel coding agents. Plans tasks, spawns agents in git worktrees, handles CI fixes, merge conflicts, and code reviews autonomously. Agent-agnostic (Claude Code, Codex, Aider). Runtime-agnostic (tmux, Docker). Web dashboard at localhost:3000.
input_format: Task descriptions, GitHub issues, backlog items
output_format: Pull requests per agent, automated CI fixes
verification_method: CI-driven verification. Automatic CI failure injection and fixing. Code review routing.
human_gates: PR review as primary gate. Human notified only when judgment required. Otherwise fully autonomous.
agent_architecture: Central orchestrator (itself an AI agent) coordinates multiple coding agents. 8 swappable slots (agent, runtime, tracker, SCM, notifier). Each agent gets own git worktree and branch. 3,288 test cases.
execution_model: Central server coordinates agents. Each agent in isolated git worktree. Automatic CI failure detection and fixing. Review comment routing. Event-driven GitHub integration.
strengths: Most agent-agnostic orchestrator (Claude Code, Codex, Aider)
weaknesses: No built-in assessment/splitting for large tasks
comparison_to_forge: Agent Orchestrator is the closest competitor to Forge's execution engine specifically. Both use git worktree isolation and parallel agent execution. Key differences: Forge has DAG-based wave planning with dependency resolution; Forge has 8-layer verification vs. CI-only; Forge has session ledger for cross-wave knowledge; Forge has assessment/splitting for context management; Forge has agent factory with archetype-based specialization. Agent Orchestrator is more agent-agnostic.

name: Open SWE (LangChain)
description: Cloud-based asynchronous coding agent built on LangGraph. Multi-agent architecture with Planner, Coder, and Reviewer. Subagent orchestration for complex tasks. Integrates with Slack, Linear, GitHub for triggering. Sandbox isolation via Modal/Daytona/Runloop.
input_format: GitHub issues, Slack messages, Linear tickets
output_format: Pull requests with reviewed changes
verification_method: Dedicated Reviewer agent checks for errors, runs tests and formatters, reflects on changes before PR. Sandbox execution.
human_gates: Asynchronous messaging during execution. Can accept feedback/redirects mid-task. PR review as final gate.
agent_architecture: Multi-agent: Planner (researches codebase, forms strategy), Coder (implements), Reviewer (checks errors, runs tests, reflects). Subagent decomposition for complex tasks. Built on LangGraph Deep Agents.
execution_model: Cloud-native asynchronous execution. Multiple sandbox providers (Modal, Daytona, Runloop). Parallel task processing. Human-in-the-loop messaging during execution.
strengths: Asynchronous cloud execution - no local resources consumed
Human messaging during execution (can redirect mid-task)
Backed by LangChain with enterprise support
comparison_to_forge: Open SWE's multi-agent architecture (Planner/Coder/Reviewer) is similar to Forge's agent archetypes but less specialized. Open SWE's async execution with human messaging is more flexible than Forge's phase gates. Forge has deeper verification (8 layers vs. single reviewer), session continuity, and DAG-based planning. Open SWE has better integration breadth (Slack, Linear, GitHub).

name: Mentat
description: AI coding assistant for coordinated multi-file edits from the command line. Unlike Copilot, coordinates across files. Project context-aware without copy-pasting. ARCHIVED Jan 2025 - team pivoted to GitHub bot product (mentat.ai).
input_format: Natural language instructions, file context
output_format: Multi-file code edits
verification_method: None built-in
human_gates: Interactive approval of changes
agent_architecture: Single agent with project context awareness. Multi-file editing coordination.
